title: Developer Lab: Conversational Fallbacks & SDK Adaptor Scratch
content:
Purpose
This is a working lab document capturing a pragmatic PRD-level sketch and experiment plan for two tightly coupled goals: (1) provide a clear SDK adaptor surface that lets client apps express progressive, structured tool calls during streaming responses, and (2) define a deterministic, observable fallback system for intermittent network and model-fidelity regressions that minimizes developer integration work.

Why this matters
- Developers building interactive features (search assistants, in-product help flows, automation) need predictable fallback behavior when streaming partial outputs or calling tools.
- Current SDK surfaces are inconsistent across languages; teams often reimplement ad-hoc client-side reconcilers.
- We can reduce rework and customer incidents if the SDK provides an opinionated adaptor for partial structured frames + an explicit fallback policy with telemetry hooks.

Non-goals
- Not shipping a final API today; this is lab->prototype->playbook path.
- Not replacing advanced orchestration (A/B rollouts, heavy-weight canaries) — aim for a low-lift building block.

High-level design constraints
- Backwards-compatible with existing hosted streaming endpoints (must accept incremental frames).
- Minimal runtime dependencies in client SDKs; prefer a small adaptor shim that apps can opt into.
- Telemetry-first: every fallback decision must emit a structured event (traceable to request id, model variant, client sdk version).
- Latency budget: any client-side recovery should not add > 50ms median overhead in the common-case.

User journeys (examples)
1) Mobile sales assistant with flaky connectivity
  - User starts a streaming request to generate an email draft with a requested calendar check (tool call).
  - Partial response contains: plain text intro, then tool-call intent, then tool results.
  - Network drops mid-tool-call; SDK should surface the partial draft to UI, queue the pending tool-call for retry, and emit a single 'session-fallback' event.
  - App displays a lightweight 'Resume background sync' notice and continues to allow edits.

2) Web customer-support UI where model falls back to cheaper variant
  - App requests high-fidelity model but the routing layer falls back to a smaller variant due to capacity.
  - The SDK adaptor should detect structured output mismatch (e.g., missing fields) and either synthesize placeholders or request a short synchronous re-resolve depending on policy.

SDK adaptor surface sketch (conceptual)
- Streaming frames are normalized into three logical frame types: TEXT_DELTA, STRUCT_FRAME, TOOL_FRAME.
- Adaptor exposes a single event stream in the SDK: onFrame(frame) where frame is one of the three types; offers helper callbacks for idempotent tool calls: registerToolHandler(toolName, handlerFn).
- The adaptor provides:
  - frame.commit() — marks a frame as committed for client UI (useful for optimistic commits).
  - frame.defer(reason) — marks that client deferred processing (stored in local queue).
  - adaptor.retryQueuedTools(policy) — built-in retry with jitter/backoff options.
- Pseudocode (JS):
  const adaptor = RedwoodStreamingAdaptor(streamSocket, { onEvent });
  adaptor.registerToolHandler('calendar.lookup', async (payload) => {
    try {
      const result = await callCalendarService(payload);
      return { status: 'ok', result };
    } catch (e) {
      return { status: 'retry' }; // let adaptor decide backoff
    }
  });

Structured output and schema negotiation
- Host should include a lightweight schema hint in initial handshake (schemaId: optional). Adaptor attempts to validate STRUCT_FRAMEs against hinted schema at runtime.
- If validation fails: three policy options (configurable per client key):
  1) SYNTHESIZE: adaptor fills default placeholders into missing fields and tags result as 'synthesized'.
  2) RESOLVE_SYNC: perform a short synchronous re-resolve using a compact prompt, bounded to 300ms.
  3) EMIT_PARTIAL: surface the invalid frame as-is and mark event 'schema-mismatch'.
- Default policy for self-serve customers should be EMIT_PARTIAL to avoid hidden mutation. Enterprise default may be RESOLVE_SYNC.

Fallback taxonomy and signals
- Fallback triggers: network error, socket resume, explicit backend fallback (model variant change), tool-timeout, schema mismatch, tokenization error.
- Each trigger maps to a coarse action: QUEUE_AND_RETRY, SPOOL_TO_SERVER, SYNTHESIZE_AND_CONTINUE, ABORT_AND_NOTIFY.
- Telemetry event shape (stringified JSON in SDK):
  - event_type: fallback_decision
  - request_id, session_id, model_from, model_to, client_sdk_version
  - trigger: one of (network, backend_fallback, tool_timeout, schema_mismatch)
  - decision: action chosen
  - elapsed_ms_since_request_start
  - user_visible: true/false
  - note: short text

Developer ergonomics priorities
- Minimal required code for most flows: register 1-2 tool handlers and attach adaptor to socket.
- Provide strong debug mode: adaptor.debug(true) emits frame diffs and suggested fixes for schema mismatches.
- Local emulation harness: small npm/py package that mirrors server-side fallback triggers so integrators can simulate failure modes locally.

Experiment matrix (lab phase)
- Variant A: EMIT_PARTIAL default, SDK exposes queued-tool retry with exponential backoff.
- Variant B: RESOLVE_SYNC default with 300ms budget for schema mismatches.
- Variant C: SYNTHESIZE default for low-risk schemas and EMIT_PARTIAL for unknown.
Metrics to compare:
  - user-perceived incomplete outputs (product probe + manual labeling)
  - incidence of customer support tickets tied to streaming failures
  - 95th percentile latency for first content commit
  - fraction of fallback events marked user_visible=true

Security & privacy considerations
- Tool calls may include sensitive data (emails, calendar tokens); adaptor must enforce token redaction when emitting telemetry.
- Default telemetry redaction: drop tool payloads, include only toolName + outcome + hashes for correlation.
- Enterprise customers can opt-in to full telemetry export (via secure endpoint) under contract.

Rollout plan (alpha -> beta -> GA)
- Alpha (developer-lab): internal SDKs (JS + Python) + emulation harness; surface as experimental flag for power customers. 6 weeks.
- Beta: enable self-serve opt-in in console, add mobile SDK wrappers, expand telemetry retention to 30 days. 8 weeks.
- GA: default available, documented using playbook; provide migration guide for customers currently doing ad-hoc reconcilers. 12+ weeks.

Acceptance criteria (for Beta)
- SDK adaptor implemented in JS + Python with registerToolHandler and retry queue.
- Emulation harness covers at least 5 failure modes.
- Telemetry events emitted for 100% of fallback decisions and visible in Console trace view.
- No more than 2% increase in median response time for integrated clients vs baseline.

Open questions / TODOs
- Need product decision on default schema-mismatch policy for self-serve vs enterprise. (Priya to pick by 2025-03-05)
- How to version schema hints; propose semantic id (schema:v1) — research whether we can piggyback on model metadata. (Liam)
- Server-side primitive for 're-resolve short prompt' (RESOLVE_SYNC) — can the router enforce the 300ms budget? Ops requirement.
- Mobile persistence model for queued tool calls on app background vs force-quit. (Diego)

Quick developer checklist (for integrator)
- [ ] Add RedwoodStreamingAdaptor to client project (npm/pypi experimental package).
- [ ] registerToolHandler for each tool the model may request.
- [ ] attach onFrame handler to update UI progressively and call frame.commit() for durable UI updates.
- [ ] enable adaptor.debug(true) in staging to collect frame diffs.
- [ ] run emulation harness locally for network drop and backend-fallback scenarios.

Notes to self
- Keep this doc loose; follow-up PRD should include concrete API specs (wire-level JSON for frames), SDK method signatures with typed examples, and a small integration example repo.
- Schedule a 60-minute sync with SRE/Router team to validate feasibility of synchronous re-resolve budgets.

References and snippets
- Related tickets: JIRA-API-1024 (fallback telemetry), JIRA-API-1100 (schema hints), CONFLUENCE-1482 (streaming frame taxonomy).
- Local experiment repo: github.com/redwood-inference/hosted-sdk-lab (WIP).

-- end of sketch --
